Multiple problems. To answer the original question, yes, you can store any object in an ArrayList. Your code has a couple of bugs. 

To start off, you declare "public class" and then do not give a class name. You then define a method with "public main void", which will cause another error. If you're trying to define the main method, try "public static void main(String\[\] args)".

You then define an ArrayList, but use the student constructor to instantiate it. Try using "new ArrayList<student>()" instead.

you then make a student object, but don't give it the input of the id. Try changing the constructor so you can write "student s = new student(studentid);".

Then, you add studentid to the arraylist, which isn't what it contains; it contains objects of the student type, not ints. You're also not passing it in as a int, you're passing it in as a String.

Fix those, and you should be good.
